tools.name: codekit-ast-detail
tools.description: [FILE AST DETAIL] Inspect one or more exact source files and return plain Markdown AST details. Use this only after you already know the exact files, typically from codekit-ast-tree or codekit-rg.

parameters.name: paths
parameters.description: One or more explicit source-file paths separated by newlines (\n). This tool does not accept directories or mixed path sets, and it supports at most 20 files per request.

parameters.name: comment
parameters.description: Include condensed comment summaries for functions in the structural output (default: false). Separator-style comment banners and metadata-only lines such as params/returns are filtered out, and each summary is compressed to a short single-line note.

tools.prompt:
CRITICAL RULES:
- USE THIS ONLY when you already know the exact source files. Do NOT guess or hallucinate paths.
- INPUT: Pass explicit file paths in `paths`, separated by newlines. Max 20 files. Directories are rejected.
- COMMENTS: Keep `comment=false` by default. Enable it only when condensed function-note summaries are truly needed.
- OUTPUT: Returns plain Markdown text.
- OVERFLOW: If the result exceeds the safe inline budget, inline content is omitted. Follow the returned raw-file pointer and chunked read plan.

tools.name: codekit-rg
tools.description: [TEXT-TO-STRUCTURE BRIDGE] Use this after you have a text signal or regex target. Search a directory with ripgrep, then return only the directly relevant function/class AST context as plain Markdown.

parameters.name: dir
parameters.description: Target directory to search recursively. This parameter is required for a fresh search and must point to an existing directory.

parameters.name: ext
parameters.description: Optional file-extension filter, comma-separated (for example lua,rs,ts). You may also pass common language names such as rust or typescript, which are normalized to their corresponding file extensions. When omitted, codekit-rg uses the same built-in source-code default set as codekit-ast-detail and excludes non-core formats such as css/html/json/yaml.

parameters.name: noignore
parameters.description: Disable ignore rules only when set to true. Leave it unset for the normal ignored-by-default search behavior.

parameters.name: rg_pattern
parameters.description: Ripgrep regex used for the first-pass text search. This parameter is required for a fresh search.

tools.prompt:
CRITICAL RULES:
- WORKFLOW: Use this after identifying a text signal or regex target. Do NOT use it for first-pass repository exploration.
- INPUT: `dir` must be a directory and `rg_pattern` is required. `ext` is a file-extension filter; common language names are normalized automatically.
- IGNORE: Leave ignored paths enabled by default. Set `noignore=true` only when you explicitly need ignored directories.
- OUTPUT: Return only the directly relevant structure context plus matched lines; do not expand full function bodies.
- OVERFLOW: If the result exceeds the safe inline budget, inline content is omitted. Follow the returned raw-file pointer and chunked read plan.

tools.name: codekit-markdown-menu
tools.description: [MARKDOWN MENU] Triage Markdown files by headings only. Use this to locate the right docs file or section before reading body text elsewhere.

parameters.name: path
parameters.description: Target path. Supports a single file/directory, or multiple paths separated by newlines (\n). Directory and file paths may be mixed in one request and duplicate Markdown files are automatically removed.

parameters.name: recursive
parameters.description: Whether to recurse into subdirectories when a directory is encountered (default: false). Keep this false for top-level doc triage and enable it only when you need nested Markdown files.

parameters.name: noignore
parameters.description: Disable ignore rules only when set to true. Leave it unset for the normal ignored-by-default documentation scan behavior.

tools.prompt:
CRITICAL RULES:
- PURPOSE: Use only for Markdown triage and navigation. It does NOT summarize body text.
- INPUT: `path` accepts files, directories, or mixed newline-separated paths. Duplicate Markdown files are removed automatically.
- RECURSION: Keep `recursive=false` for first-pass top-level triage. Enable it only when diving into a smaller docs subtree.
- IGNORE: Leave ignored paths enabled by default. Set `noignore=true` only when you explicitly need ignored docs.
- LIMITATION: No cache and no export. If the client truncates the response, narrow the path scope and call the tool again.

tools.name: codekit-ast-tree
tools.description: [DIRECTORY AST TREE] Pick candidate source files from exactly one directory before deep inspection. Returns a compact recursive Markdown tree grouped by subdirectory.

parameters.name: paths
parameters.description: Exactly one directory path. The parameter name remains `paths`, but the value must contain a single non-empty directory path only; multiple directories and file paths are rejected.

parameters.name: ext
parameters.description: Optional file-extension filter, comma-separated (for example rs,ts,tsx). You may also pass common language names such as rust or typescript, which are normalized to their corresponding file extensions. When omitted, codekit-ast-tree uses the built-in source-code default set.

parameters.name: noignore
parameters.description: Disable ignore rules only when set to true. Leave it unset for the normal ignored-by-default tree scan behavior.

tools.prompt:
CRITICAL RULES:
- PURPOSE: Use this for repository-level file picking before `codekit-ast-detail`.
- INPUT STRICTNESS: Pass exactly one directory path in `paths`. Multiple paths or explicit files are rejected.
- BEHAVIOR: Always recursive. Use `ext` to narrow the file-extension scope when the tree is too noisy.
- IGNORE: Leave ignored paths enabled by default. Set `noignore=true` only when you explicitly need ignored trees such as target or dist.
- NEXT STEP: Use the grouped output to choose exact files for `codekit-ast-detail` or `codekit-rg`.
- OVERFLOW: If the result exceeds the safe inline budget, inline content is omitted. Follow the returned raw-file pointer and chunked read plan.

tools.name: codekit-patch
tools.description: [FUNCTION AST PATCH] Replace one function or method by structural selector. Use this only for full-function replacement when raw line edits are unsafe or stale.

parameters.name: file
parameters.description: Target file that contains the function to patch. This parameter is required and must point to a regular file.

parameters.name: selector
parameters.description: Flexible structural selector for a function or method, for example with_vmm, McpServer/with_vmm, or impl McpServer/with_vmm. If multiple nodes match, the tool returns more specific candidates instead of patching blindly.

parameters.name: replacement
parameters.description: Replacement source text. It must be the complete function source, starting from the declaration line. Body-only fragments are rejected.

tools.prompt:
CRITICAL RULES:
- SCOPE: Replaces only function or method nodes. Never target type names or field identifiers.
- STRICT REPLACEMENT: `replacement` must contain the complete function source from declaration to closing delimiter. Body-only fragments are rejected.
- RESOLUTION: Start with a loose `selector`. If multiple nodes match, use the returned candidates to refine the next call.
- SAFETY: The tool validates the patched file with AST re-scan and error-node checks before accepting the write.

prompts.name: vulcan_codekit_skill
prompts.description: Best-practice workflow for choosing codekit tools, with an optional task string appended as the user's current instruction.

arguments.name: task
arguments.description: Optional current task or intent. Prompt completions provide common analysis and editing workflows; when provided, it is appended as a follow-up user message after the shared guidance.
completions: Analyze the current project and summarize its structure, main modules, and key responsibilities
Search the project for a function name, keyword, log string, or regex clue and identify the owning function or class
Inspect the selected source files in AST detail and summarize the key symbols and signatures
Scan the Markdown documentation and locate the most relevant file or heading section for the current topic
Prepare for a safe full-function or full-method replacement by locating the exact owner and current implementation
Map an unfamiliar source directory first, then identify which files should be inspected or delegated next
